newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Red chips outperform HK stock index, hit records.
newsitem.headline: Red chips outperform HK stock index, hit records.

text.p: Red chips, Hong Kong registered and listed China-backed companies, staged strong gains on Thursday with at least 10 of them hitting record or year highs.
Analysts said news of spin-offs and asset injections at some of the companies and hopes that they would be beneficiaries of Hong Kong's 1997 handover boosted the red chips.

"They are now expensive but fundamentally some of them should be able to go higher especially on the current bullish market sentiment," said Andrew Kuet at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell Asia Securities (HK) Ltd.
CITIC Pacific Ltd, Guangdong Investment Ltd, China Resources Enterprise Ltd, Ng Fung Hong Ltd, China Overseas Land & Investment Ltd and Guangnan Holdings Ltd all hit their all time highs on Thursday.

Those reached or rose above their year highs included Guangzhou Investment Co Ltd, China Travel International Investment H.K. Ltd, China Aerospace International Holdings Ltd and Shougang Concord Technology Holdings Ltd.
Some fund managers and analysts said foreign money was the main steam for the recent red chips rally since many of the local funds had been fully weighted.
"I believe some of this money is from China because the Chinese government want to see a robust stock market here at next year's handover," an analyst said.
Hong Kong will revert to China on July 1, 1997 after being ruled by the British colonial government for more than 150 years.
